page: Hetzner Cloud cax11 is an entry-level, Arm64-based virtual server belonging to the cax server family. It is provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor and features 2 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, utilizing 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core, and includes 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the cax11 is positioned for lightweight workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is average at 1821.28, while multi-core performance falls into the weak category at 3610.67. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with read-only large block speeds at 25.88 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.72 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect similar constraints, yielding a single-core score of 1053.0 and a multi-core score of 1905.0. Database and web serving capabilities are modest, with Redis SET operations reaching 2.58 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 2.46 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cax11 offers a highly economical entry point into Arm64 cloud computing, trading dedicated CPU performance and high memory bandwidth for low-cost resource availability. Due to its shared CPU architecture and limited memory capacity, it is not suitable for resource-intensive tasks like large-scale LLM inference or heavy compilation. Instead, the server is best suited for lightweight applications, including basic web serving, development and testing environments, small database operations, and simple background task processing.

Powered by the QEMU hypervisor, it features 2 shared vCPUs from an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM and 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark data indicates modest performance, with average single-core CPU capabilities but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth results. The server lacks dedicated GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Qualitatively, the cax11 represents a highly cost-efficient option for developers seeking to test Arm64 architectures or run low-demand services. It is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight background processes, small database operations, and development environments.
